title: Opt-in shadow shim and rollback criteria for protocol consolidation
creator: Maya Patel
description: PRD for an opt-in shadowing compatibility shim and a clear rollback/stop criteria to enable safe consolidation of older transport endpoints into the unified inference API. Goal: let client SDKs and selected customers opt-in to mirrored traffic to the new protocol without impacting production latency or success rate, collect deterministic telemetry and QA outputs, and provide automated rollback triggers if regressions are detected.
scope:
In scope: gateway-level opt-in 'shadow' mirror that duplicates requests to the new endpoint variant, lightweight request adapter (shim) to normalize legacy payloads, SDK opt-in flag and CLI, telemetry dashboards for correctness/latency/error delta, rollout gating and automatic traffic cutover playbook.
Out of scope: mandatory client migration, full protocol translation library for all deprecated endpoints, and long-term removal timeline (handled in separate deprecation ticket).
success_metrics: >=95% parity on response signature and status codes between production and shadow for opt-in clients
Median extra latency introduced for mirrored requests < 2ms (shadow path only, no added latency to production responses)
Telemetry coverage: 100% of mirrored requests instrumented with trace IDs and diff payloads
No customer-facing error rate increase attributable to the shim during pilot
acceptance_criteria: Gateway implements a non-blocking mirror mode behind an opt-in flag: documented Boolean config and rollout API
SDKs (python/js/go) expose a stable API flag (client.migration_shadow = true) and ship adapters that convert legacy body/headers into unified request format
Dashboards live: parity dashboard (status-code delta, schema diffs), latency heatmap, error regression panel, and per-client telemetry breakdown
Automated alert rules created: stop-and-rollback triggers when 5xx delta > 0.5% absolute or per-client parity < 90% for 30m rolling window
End-to-end test harness that replays recorded requests into shadow and verifies deterministic outputs for a configurable assertion set
Migration playbook doc published (Confluence) with step-by-step for support, SRE, and SEs, including rollback steps and public client communication templates
Pilot completed with at least 3 distinct customers and 2 internal SDK integrations without triggering rollback
dependencies: ENG-22491 (gateway-mirroring-runtime): gateway hooking and non-blocking mirror pipeline
ENG-22910 (sdk-adapters): SDK adapter implementations and release
ENG-23187 (telemetry-pipeline): trace propagation and diff event schema
PM-15234 (versioned-routing-telemetry): alignment on routing and telemetry contracts
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Patel: Draft PRD created; primary risk is shadow-induced resource usage and noisy diffs from non-deterministic models. Planning a soft quota on mirrored requests during pilot.

2026-03-06 Connor Blake: Eng sync — agreed to amortize mirror CPU/memory by sampling 10% of traffic for pilot and 100% for opt-in clients. ENG requested explicit trace-id propagation; added as dependency.
2026-03-10 Design review (Aisha Chen): UX for SDK opt-in flag should be minimal — prefer environment variable + explicit method. Logged design note at https://go.redwood.design/shadow-sdk-optin

2026-03-11 Legal (R. Alvarez): Confirmed that mirrored payloads will be treated as ephemeral telemetry and not persisted; KMS policy review required if customer opts to mirror PII — added security_review_required
2026-03-12 Engineering (PR): initial gateway PoC landed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1245 — performance results look promising, extra CPU ~3% at 10% sampled mirror

2026-03-14 PM update: Added rollback thresholds after SRE comment — if parity < 90% for any pilot client for >30m, automation will disable mirror for that client and page the PM/owner. Next steps: finalize dashboard queries and CI replay harness.
notes: This ticket is intended to de-risk the consolidation of legacy endpoints by offering a reversible, observable migration path for clients. The shim must be strictly non-blocking for production responses and must emit minimal additional latency. Plan to iterate on sampling and quotas after pilot learnings.
